Control theory

Open loop and closed loop

Open loop: no measurement

The code picks an output and sends it.

Nothing measures the result.

A change in battery, friction or load goes uncorrected.

Closed loop: measure and correct

The code sends an output and reads a sensor.

It compares the reading with the target and corrects.

That measurement is called feedback.

Arm angle (degrees from flat)

1

Flat is hardest

The bar sticks straight out, so gravity’s lever is longest: 1.21 V.

2

The cosine

At 45° it takes 0.85 V. Straight up it takes 0 V. Your calculator’s cos does this.

3

Why 0° is flat

Then cos(0) = 1, and kG simply means “volts to hold it flat”.

Deck 6 · Arm PID

11

Control theory

Where 1.21 volts comes from

1

Gravity torque when flat: 15.7 N·m

Mass × g × distance to the middle: 4 × 9.8 × 0.4.

2

Torque at the NEO: 0.261 N·m

The gearbox divides it by 60.

3

Current for that torque: 10.6 A

Divide by the NEO’s 0.0248 N·m per amp.

4

Volts to push that current: 1.21 V

Multiply by the NEO’s 0.114 ohms. The motor is not turning, so it makes no voltage of its own.

Feedforward does the work. PID cleans up.

Feedforward is the volts you can predict. PID handles only what you could not.

Deck 6 · Arm PID

14

Control theory

The rest of feedforward: kS and kV

ArmFeedforward(kS, kG, kV) adds all three. You already know the middle one.

kS: friction

The volts needed to overcome friction and start moving.

kG: gravity

1.21 V × cos(angle) on our arm.

kV: speed

Back-EMF grows with speed. Our arm takes 1.19 V per rad/s of speed.

Deck 6 · Arm PID

17

Control theory

Tuning steps, in order

1

kG first

All gains at 0. Raise kG until the arm stays where you leave it.

2

kS, only if needed

If the arm sticks and then jumps, add a small kS.

3

Raise kP

Start low and raise it in steps. Stop when it starts to overshoot.

4

Add kD

Add D until the overshoot goes. If the motor buzzes, back off.

5

Test with small, safe moves

Try 10° before 90°. Hand on the disable key, every time.

The same arm, written two ways

Deck 6 · Arm PID

20

Best practice

One unit in Java, convert at the boundary

Pick one unit for all your Java: radians. Convert once, where the code meets the hardware.

The SPARK reports rotations, so ArmUnits is the only class that converts. Hold the arm flat and save the raw reading as ENCODER_FLAT_ROTATIONS.

public static double encoderToArmRad(double encoderRotations) {

  double turnsFromFlat = encoderRotations - ENCODER_FLAT_ROTATIONS;

  return MathUtil.angleModulus(Units.rotationsToRadians(turnsFromFlat));

}

public static double armRadToMotorRotations(double armRad) {

  return Units.radiansToRotations(armRad) * GEAR_RATIO;

}

21

Programming

The loop on the roboRIO

ArmSubsystem.java

// A NEO is brushless. kBrushed would damage it.

private final SparkMax motor = new SparkMax(MOTOR_ID, MotorType.kBrushless);

private final SparkAbsoluteEncoder throughBore = motor.getAbsoluteEncoder();

private final PIDController pid = new PIDController(KP, 0, KD);

private final ArmFeedforward feedforward = new ArmFeedforward(KS, KG, KV);

 

/** Runs every 20 ms. Feedforward holds, PID fixes the rest. */

private void driveToTarget() {

  double angle = getAngleRad();

  double ffVolts = feedforward.calculate(angle, 0.0);

  double pidVolts = pid.calculate(angle, targetRad);

  double volts = ffVolts + pidVolts;

  lastVolts = MathUtil.clamp(volts, -MAX_VOLTS, MAX_VOLTS);

  motor.setVoltage(lastVolts);

}

Command factories: moveTo and holdPosition

ArmSubsystem.java

  /** Near the goal for 0.1 s in a row. */

1 public final Trigger atGoal =

1     new Trigger(pid::atSetpoint).debounce(0.1);

   

  public Command moveTo(double goalRad) {

2   double goal =

2       MathUtil.clamp(goalRad, SOFT_MIN_RAD, SOFT_MAX_RAD);

3   return startRun(() -> startMove(goal), this::driveToTarget)

        .until(atGoal)

        .withName("Arm moveTo");

  }

   

4 public Command holdPosition() {

4   return startRun(this::startHold, this::driveToTarget)

        .withName("Arm hold");

  }

1

atGoal

A Trigger that needs 0.1 s near the goal, so one lucky reading does not count.

2

Clamp the goal

A bad setpoint gets stopped here, before the motor sees it.

3

Start clean

Sync the encoders, reset PID, then loop until atGoal.

4

Hold

Keep the last goal if the arm got there. If not, hold where it is.

23

Programming

A default command that holds, and triggers

RobotContainer.java

private void configureBindings() {

  // With nothing else running, hold still.

  // This also stops the arm jumping when you enable.

  arm.setDefaultCommand(arm.holdPosition());

 

  driver.a().onTrue(arm.moveTo(STOW_RAD));

  driver.y().onTrue(arm.moveTo(SCORE_RAD));

 

  // A Trigger can watch the arm, not just a button.

  // This only fires if the arm has arrived.

  driver.rightBumper().and(arm.atGoal).onTrue(Commands.print("Score!"));

}

The bumper fires only when the driver presses it and the arm has arrived.

1

The trapezoid

Top speed 2.5 rad/s, acceleration 6 rad/s².

2

One step

Each loop, the setpoint moves a little toward the goal.

3

kV gets a speed

The profile knows the target speed, so feedforward can use it.

Best practice

Safety goes in before tuning

Add soft limits, a current limit and an output clamp first. Keep people clear and a hand on the disable key.

Start with low gains. On the Driver Station, Enter disables and Space is the emergency stop.

// NEO rotations, because the NEO's encoder is the selected sensor.

config.softLimit

    .forwardSoftLimit(armRadToMotorRotations(SOFT_MAX_RAD))

    .forwardSoftLimitEnabled(true)

    .reverseSoftLimit(armRadToMotorRotations(SOFT_MIN_RAD))

    .reverseSoftLimitEnabled(true);

Deck 6 · Arm PID

28

Common mistake

The arm runs away at full speed

What you see

You enable, and the arm slams to a stop as fast as it can go.

Why it happens

Motor and encoder disagree on direction. Moving “toward” the goal makes the error bigger, so P pushes harder.

The fix

Robot disabled: lift the arm by hand. The angle must go up. Then at about 1 V: the arm must rise. Flip ENCODER_INVERTED or MOTOR_INVERTED.

Deck 6 · Arm PID

29

Common mistakes

Five more gotchas, by symptom

What you seeWhy it happensThe fix
Ask for 45 and the arm drives to its top limitWrong units: 45 radians is about 7 turnsUse Units.degreesToRadians
Arm leans on a stop and the motor gets hotSetpoint out of range, so error never reaches 0Clamp goals to the soft limits
Always off by the same ratioGear ratio wrong in ArmUnitsTurn the arm 90° by hand and check
Correct at first, off after a restartRelative encoder, no homing: it reads 0 at power-onUse the absolute encoder, or home on a stop
Arm sags more with kG, 3.5° not 1.7°kG sign backwards: up is negative in your codeMake up positive and keep kG positive

And I windup: if the arm overshoots after being stuck, cap I with setIntegratorRange or leave it out.
